title: Crusoe to deploy AI cloud in Paraguay powered by the Itaipu dam
content:
Crusoe Partners with Araico to Deploy AI Cloud Infrastructure in Paraguay
Powered by Itaipú Hydroelectric Dam, new partnership brings 100% renewable energy to power Crusoe Cloud
PARAGUAY — October 22, 2026 — Crusoe, the AI factory company, today announced a strategic partnership with Paraguayan energy and infrastructure developer Araico to build high-performance AI compute infrastructure powered by the Itaipú Hydroelectric Dam. Building on Crusoe’s established energy-first strategy, the initiative marks Crusoe’s first dedicated AI Cloud deployment in Latin America. This project advances the company’s approach of locating AI compute directly at abundant energy sources worldwide.
Under the partnership, Crusoe plans to bring an initial deployment online in mid-2027, with a path to scale to 106 MW of IT capacity and long-term options to expand to approximately 280 MW total. Located adjacent to the Itaipú substation, the facility will tap directly into one of the largest and most reliable 100% renewable hydroelectric power sources in the world, and will serve both U.S. cloud customers and growing in-region demand across Latin America through Crusoe Cloud.
Paraguay’s President Santiago Peña said: “This partnership between Crusoe and Araico directly unlocks new value from our natural resources. It brings jobs, investment, technology, and innovation to Paraguay, and gives us a scalable model to create meaningful, lasting change for the Paraguayan people. This is an opportunity for Paraguay to establish itself as a regional leader in AI infrastructure.”
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, who was leading a U.S. business delegation in Paraguay when the agreement was signed, hailed its historic scope and significance. “Paraguay’s abundant hydroelectric energy creates enormous opportunities for economic growth and jobs, and I’m delighted that American capital and know-how will establish Paraguay as a world-class tech powerhouse,” said Landau. “This project has the potential to be the largest private foreign investment in Paraguayan history and reinforces the strong and longstanding bonds between our countries.”
“Crusoe was founded on a simple idea: build digital infrastructure where power is abundant, accessible and environmentally-aligned,” said Cully Cavness, Co-founder, President, and Chief Strategy Officer of Crusoe. “Paraguay’s unique history and geography have enabled one of the most abundant renewable power sources in the world through the Itaipú Hydroelectric Dam. Crusoe’s energy-first strategy is designed precisely to unlock and add value to this kind of power resource through advanced digital infrastructure. On behalf of the whole Crusoe team, we look forward to making this project a success for the people of Paraguay, for our local partners and for Crusoe.”
Crusoe's approach in Paraguay pairs local infrastructure development expertise with Crusoe's AI factory and cloud operations track record. Araico will lead local development and site infrastructure adjacent to the Itaipú substation, while Crusoe will manage, operate, and deliver the physical compute for Crusoe Cloud.
“Partnering with Crusoe brings world-class AI infrastructure to Paraguay while showcasing our nation’s renewable energy leadership on a global scale,” said Alejandro Zuccolillo, CEO of Araico. “By pairing Itaipú’s massive hydroelectric capacity with Crusoe’s ability to build and manage AI infrastructure, we are capturing maximum value from Paraguay's renewable power right here at home, and transforming our energy abundance into high-tech industrial growth, local jobs, and digital innovation.”
The Paraguay deployment strengthens Crusoe's growing global footprint of energy-aligned AI infrastructure, extending its reach across North America, Europe, and now Latin America while deepening digital infrastructure ties throughout the Western Hemisphere.
About Crusoe
As the AI factory company, Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. The company provides a reliable, scalable, cost-effective, energy-first solution for AI infrastructure. By harnessing large-scale energy sources, building AI-optimized data centers, and delivering a powerful AI cloud platform, Crusoe empowers its customers and partners to build the future faster. For more information, visit crusoe.ai.
About Araico
Araico is the AI Powerhouse of Latin America. The company transforms clean hydroelectric Itaipú power into compute with the most competitive tokenomics in the world. Araico was founded on a simple conviction: the next era of human capability will be built on power that is clean, abundant, and in the right place. We exist to put it there. Learn more at araico.com.py.

report.summary: Crusoe and Araico plan a 106 MW AI cloud in Paraguay powered by the Itaipú hydroelectric dam, scaling toward 280 MW.
report.background: AI demand is growing faster than available power in many traditional data-center markets. Grid interconnection queues, land constraints, and sustainability goals are pushing operators to locate compute directly at large energy sources. Crusoe has pursued an energy-first strategy, building AI factories near abundant or stranded power. Paraguay offers one of the world's largest hydroelectric resources through Itaipú, but the country wants to convert cheap renewable electricity into higher-value industrial activity. The deal also reflects a broader trend: AI infrastructure is becoming a geopolitically significant export, with U.S. companies seeking friendly locations and Latin American governments courting investment. Crusoe's Paraguay entry would be its first dedicated AI cloud in Latin America, extending a footprint already spanning North America and Europe.
key_points: Crusoe and Araico plan an initial AI cloud deployment in Paraguay for mid-2027, starting with a path to 106 MW of IT capacity and long-term options near 280 MW. The facility will sit next to the Itaipú substation and draw 100% renewable hydroelectric power, serving both U.S. cloud customers and Latin American demand.

Araico will handle local development and site infrastructure, while Crusoe will manage, operate, and deliver physical compute through Crusoe Cloud. The split pairs local energy and permitting knowledge with Crusoe's AI factory and cloud operations experience, a model meant to speed deployment and reduce execution risk in a new market.

The project is Crusoe's first dedicated AI Cloud deployment in Latin America and extends its energy-first footprint across North America, Europe, and now Latin America. Paraguayan officials frame it as a scalable model for jobs, investment, and regional AI leadership; a U.S. official says it could become the largest private foreign investment in Paraguayan history.

The project illustrates a shift in AI infrastructure strategy: instead of chasing traditional data-center markets, operators are siting compute at abundant power sources. Itaipú's scale and reliability make Paraguay attractive, while the deal gives the country a way to monetize surplus renewable energy and build high-tech industry rather than exporting electricity alone.
report.impact: The deal reinforces that power availability, not just chips, is becoming the binding constraint for AI expansion. If it succeeds, more AI capacity may be built in Latin America and other renewable-rich regions, diversifying the global compute map and pressuring traditional data-center hubs. For developers, it could mean additional cloud capacity with renewable attributes and potentially different pricing or latency profiles, though access and performance will depend on network links. For regular users, the main effects are indirect: more supply could ease AI service constraints over time, while local communities may see jobs and investment. It also raises questions about energy exports, grid use, and equitable benefits.
report.tools: To follow this space, watch Crusoe Cloud for commercial capacity and Araico for local project updates. For hands-on learning about AI infrastructure, open-source tools include Kubernetes or Slurm for orchestration, Ray for distributed workloads, vLLM for inference serving, Terraform for infrastructure as code, and Prometheus with Grafana for monitoring. These are not specific to Crusoe, but they reflect the software stack used to run and observe modern AI compute.
